Q0209

“When the age changes, affairs change; when affairs change, preparations must change.” — Han Feizi (Han Feizi, Five Vermin)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Han Feizi, Five Vermin. Theme: time.

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Han Feizi, Five Vermin and files it under Legalism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Han Feizi

Han Feizi (c. 280–233 BCE) was the major synthesizer of Legalism (fajia) in late Warring States China.

How to read this passage

Is time a river, a dimension, or a structure of consciousness? Augustine, Bergson, and modern metaphysics offer rival pictures while ethics asks how finite time should be spent. This passage enters that discussion through time, power.

Concepts in this quote

Time
Philosophy of time asks what tense and duration are—and how memory, death, and history shape a human life.
Power
Power is the capacity to affect others and to shape what counts as possible—central to politics and ethics.
